title: Web Development Essentials
description: Test your foundational knowledge of HTML5, modern CSS3 styling, JavaScript core concepts, and web protocols.

questions.text: What does CSS stand for in web development?
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. The 'Cascading' refers to the specific order and specificity rules governing which styles apply.

questions.text: Which HTML5 element represents the primary navigation links of a document?
questions.explanation: The <nav> element is semantic HTML5 designed specifically for major navigation blocks such as menus and tables of contents.

questions.text: CSS Flexbox is designed primarily for two-dimensional grid layouts with rows and columns.
questions.explanation: False! Flexbox is primarily one-dimensional (either row OR column). CSS Grid is the layout module designed specifically for 2D layouts.

title: Cosmic Science & Planetary Wonders
description: Journey through the cosmos with questions covering our solar system, physics, stars, and space exploration.

questions.text: Which planet in our solar system has the highest number of confirmed moons?
questions.explanation: Saturn leads the solar system with 146 recognized moons (surpassing Jupiter as of recent astronomical observations).

questions.text: Approximately how long does light from the Sun take to reach Earth?
questions.explanation: Traveling at roughly 300,000 km/s over an average distance of 150 million km, sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

questions.text: Sound travels faster through a vacuum in outer space than through Earth's atmosphere.
questions.explanation: False! Sound requires a physical medium (molecules) to travel. In the vacuum of space, sound cannot travel at all.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for Gold on the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word for gold, 'aurum', which means 'shining dawn'.

questions.text: The Apollo 11 moon landing occurred in the year 1969.
questions.explanation: True! Astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969.
